body:
I am aware this is taken word-for-word from the original description, but if you think about it, this information is rather redundant and doesn't even tell the full story.

That's because:
- The class *itself* does not support WAV, Ogg, and MP3. It's like saying "_Textures support gradients (via GradientTexture2D)_". If you stretch the meaning it's true, but it's a bit strange.
- The list of classes inheriting AudioStream can be seen right in the class reference.
- The class (and ResourceImporter?) can be inherited to support more formats if desired.

I'm not sure what exactly to do here. Perhaps the redundancy here is fine, so I wouldn't remove this line outright. At least mentioning the fact that more formats _could_ be supported may be a good idea.

This is always nasty to get around. It's a game engine, so it's too easy to misunderstand what the "player" is here, even for a brief moment.

Also, I am aware it derives from the original description, but in my opinion it doesn't make sense to say "play back" here because the audio is played in real-time.

```suggestion
		When [AudioStreamMicrophone] is used directly in an [AudioStreamPlayer] node, the audio stream player can play audio from an input device (a microphone for example) in real-time. This can be used in conjunction with [AudioEffectRecord] or [AudioEffectCapture] to save the data or process it.
```

Thank you for taking the time to review. I'll use this comment to target the overrall review you made, as well as the specific comment.
I might also comment on several of these over time, basically giving my thoughts on a specific change, and asking for confirmation on whether I should change to your suggestion or not. Sorry for the "spam". No need to reply as soon as they appear.

> As I understand, the PR isn't meant to standardize this side of the class reference, but given that it affects so much at once, it should be expected.

It wasn't exactly my goal, but I guess it's a byproduct of trying to make these files a bit more consistent. I may have failed in that, But I don't believe so much in keeping the way things were, since one could question why some descriptions for the same thing are different, and assume they work in different ways, rather than just being a documentation inconsistency. This is not me pushing back suggestions, just offering my thoughts on that line.

> There's also a lot of cases where "this audio stream" was changed to "the stream" and I am frankly not sure why, other than preference.

It's an attempt on trying to reduce unnecessary verbosity. It's an audio class, I think the "audio" part is implied enough, and saying "audio stream" all the time feels repetitive, to me at least. I could either revert those changes, or use "audio stream" for most/all instances of "stream".

-

Now for your specific comment:
In `AudioStream`, I tried to only use "Override this method [...]" when I mention a class method later on.
I'll say that I didn't try to change the phrasing for overridable methods in all files, because usually I prefer to stay close to the original phrasing.

My options for this are:
- Reverting to the original phrasing in all files, just changing what's necessary, avoiding thoughts of "consistency"
- Use "overridable method" in all overridable methods in all relevant files
- Use "override this method [...]" in all overridable methods in all relevant files

Not sure which one you'd prefer

body: The "Ideally [...]" part? I fail to see how `beat_count` is tied to sample rate. I ask you to explain this one to me. Though if we keep it, I don't think `AudioStreamWAV` is the best example, since that stream does not have `beat_count`. But the MP3 and OggVorbis streams do not have exposed methods for sample rate either. Personally, I'd say removing that reference is best. Not sure if the example is really needed, since whoever is overriding that method would know how to access the sample rate for their format/stream. I think another good option would be a reference to the unexposed methods. For example: `AudioStreamPlaybackOggVorbis::get_stream_sampling_rate()`. This is already done somewhere else in the file.
